extraction.name: COMMONSENSE QA
extraction.description: A challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering.
extraction.creator: Alon Talmor, Jonathan Herzig, Nicholas Lourie, Jonathan Berant
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Crowd-workers are asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in tum between each of the target concepts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Triplets from CONCEPTNET were filtered based on general relations, length, language, and edit distance.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: AMT workers saw, for every question set, the question concept and three answer concepts. They were asked to formulate three questions, where all questions contain the question concept. Each question should have as an answer one of the answer concepts, but not the other two.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: A disjoint group of workers verified the generated questions by annotating them as unanswerable or choosing the right answer.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Questions often require background knowledge that is trivial to humans but is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias.

name.evidence: We present C OMMONSENSE QA: a challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering.

description.evidence: To investigate question answering with prior knowledge, we present C OMMONSENSE QA: a challenging new dataset for commonsense question answering.

url.evidence: The dataset can be downloaded from www.tau-nlp.org/commonsenseqa .

inLanguage.evidence: We filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Crowd-workers are asked to author multiple-choice questions that mention the source concept and discriminate in tum between each of the target concepts.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: We ask crowdsourcing workers to author three questions per subgraph (one per target concept), to add two additional distractors per question, and to verify questions’ quality.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We extract from C ONCEPT NET(Speer et al., 2017) multiple target concepts that have the same semantic relation to a single source concept.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: 1. We filter triplets with general relations (e.g., RelatedTo ) or relations that are already well-explored in NLP (e.g., IsA). In total we use 22 relations. 2. We filter triplets where one of the concepts is more than four words or not in English. 3. We filter triplets where the edit distance between c1andc2is too low.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: AMT workers saw, for every question set, the question concept and three answer concepts. They were asked to formulate three questions, where all questions contain the question concept. Each question should have as an answer one of the answer concepts, but not the other two.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: We used Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers to generate and validate commonsense questions.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: We train a disjoint group of workers to verify the generated questions. Verifiers annotate a question as unanswerable, or choose the right answer. Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: Each question is verified by 2 workers, and only questions verified by at least one worker that answered correctly are used.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: Because questions are generated freely by workers, they often require background knowledge that is trivial to humans but is seldom explicitly reported on the web due to reporting bias (Gordon and Van Durme, 2013).

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We split the data into a training/development/test set with an 80/10/10 split.
